audit_scope.description: EIP-141 INVALID opcode semantics, EIP-8024 extended stack manipulation (DUPN/SWAPN/EXCHANGE), EIP-2681 transaction nonce limits, EIP-161 empty account cleanup and state bloat prevention, and EIP-7939 CLZ opcode

in_scope: INVALID opcode (0xfe) execution and gas consumption
DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE opcode execution and validation
Empty account detection and cleanup at transaction end
Conditional gas charge for calls to dead accounts
CLZ opcode execution and gas metering
out_of_scope: Compiler-level generation of INVALID opcode paths
Static analysis tooling for extended stack operations

misclassified_entities.reason: This represents internal smart contract code executing within the EVM. It is not an external entity crossing a trust boundary; it is code already loaded and running inside the EL's execution environment.

This represents a transaction that has already passed validation within the EL pipeline. It is an internal data flow, not an external entity. By the time it reaches the nonce state transition, it is already within the system boundary.

This represents the EVM execution context triggering CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes. It is an internal component of the EL, not an external entity. The CREATE operation originates from already-executing contract code within the EVM.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC / P2P Mempool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions triggering contract execution containing INVALID opcode arrive from unauthenticated external sources. The calldata and gas limit are fully attacker-controlled. The EVM must correctly handle the INVALID opcode by halting execution, reverting state, and consuming all remaining gas.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC / P2P Mempool (Nonce Validation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction submitters provide nonce values that must be validated against the 2^64-1 limit. An attacker could craft transactions with extreme nonce values attempting to overflow nonce counters or lock accounts.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transactions may invoke contracts containing INVALID (0xfe) opcodes. The EVM must guarantee that execution halts immediately, all state changes in the current call frame are reverted, and all remaining gas is consumed. In nested call contexts, only the inner frame should revert.

Transaction nonces must be validated to be strictly less than 2^64-1 before execution. Nonce increments must not overflow. CREATE/CREATE2 operations must check creator nonce and return zero (without executing initcode) if nonce is at maximum. Account locking at max nonce must be handled gracefully.
